turns.text:
# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist with Declutter Tips

A note on timing: start packing the lowest-use rooms first (storage, guest room, garage) around weeks 6–7, then work toward daily-use rooms in the final week. The kitchen and bathrooms go last.

---

## Label System

Every box gets three pieces of information written on at least two sides and the top.

**Room** — write the destination room in Oregon, not the Ohio room. This tells movers exactly where to put it and saves you re-sorting later. Use a color-coded dot sticker per room if you want a visual system: blue for bedroom, red for kitchen, green for living room, yellow for bathroom, orange for office, purple for garage/storage.

**Priority** — a number from 1 to 3. Priority 1 means open within the first 24 hours (sheets, coffee maker, dog stuff, toiletries). Priority 2 means open within the first week. Priority 3 means open whenever — seasonal items, books, decor.

**Fragility** — write FRAGILE in red marker on all sides if it contains breakables. Write HEAVY if it's books or tools. Write THIS SIDE UP with an arrow if orientation matters.

A finished label looks like: *Kitchen / P1 / FRAGILE — glasses and French press*

---

## Room-by-Room Checklist

### Kitchen
**Estimated boxes: 8–15 depending on your cookware, pantry size, and how many appliances you own.**

Pack in this order: rarely used appliances first (bread maker, stand mixer, fondue set), then pantry dry goods, then cookware, then plates and glasses, then daily-use items last.

**Declutter prompts:** Do you have duplicate gadgets? Expired spices (check every single one)? A "junk drawer" that hasn't been touched in a year? Small appliances you've used fewer than 3 times? Mismatched containers without lids?

- [ ] Small appliances (wrap each in bubble wrap or towels, fill cavities with packing paper)
- [ ] Pots and pans (nest them with paper between each; skillets can share a box if separated)
- [ ] Plates and bowls (pack vertically like records, not stacked flat — they survive better that way)
- [ ] Glasses and mugs (wrap each individually; use dish-pack boxes with cell dividers if possible)
- [ ] Baking dishes and sheet pans (wrap in paper; they can go in a wardrobe box standing up)
- [ ] Pantry dry goods (pack heavy items like canned goods in small boxes — these get very heavy fast)
- [ ] Spices (transport in a small bin you keep in the car so they don't overheat or spill)
- [ ] Knives (wrap in a dish towel, secure with rubber bands; label SHARP)
- [ ] Dish towels and pot holders (great filler material for fragile boxes)
- [ ] Cleaning supplies under the sink (many are hazmat and can't go on a moving truck — verify with your mover)
- [ ] Trash: use moving week to run down perishables. Donate canned goods to a food bank rather than moving them.

**Keep out until moving day:** coffee maker, one pot, one pan, two mugs, dish soap, sponge, paper towels, a few plates and utensils. Pack these in the "last out" box.

---

### Primary Bedroom
**Estimated boxes: 6–10 (more if you have extensive clothing or a large closet)**

- [ ] Off-season clothing (pack first, in large wardrobe boxes or vacuum bags to compress)
- [ ] Current-season clothing (wardrobe boxes make hanging clothes easy and protect them)
- [ ] Shoes (each pair in a bag or wrapped; original boxes are ideal if you kept them)
- [ ] Bedding and pillows (use your duvet as padding in a large box; compression bags save space)
- [ ] Mattress (movers handle this or buy a mattress bag — don't skip this, Oregon rain is real)
- [ ] Nightstand contents (keep medication, glasses, phone charger, and ear plugs out until moving day)
- [ ] Dresser contents (you can often leave clothes in drawers for a local move; ask your mover about interstate moves — drawers should usually be emptied to reduce weight and prevent damage)
- [ ] Jewelry and valuables (transport these yourself in the car, never on the truck)
- [ ] Wall art and mirrors (use mirror boxes; tape a large X of masking tape across glass to hold shards if it cracks)

**Declutter prompts:** The rule of thumb is if you haven't worn it in a year, it goes. Try the bin method: put "maybe" items in a box and seal it. If you don't open it for 3 weeks, donate it without looking inside.

---

### Guest Bedroom / Spare Room
**Estimated boxes: 4–8**

This room is your first packing target since it's lowest priority. Start here as early as week 7 or 8.

- [ ] Spare bedding and pillows
- [ ] Books and media (small boxes only for books — they become brutally heavy in large boxes)
- [ ] Hobby and craft supplies
- [ ] Extra furniture (decide now what goes and what gets sold or donated)
- [ ] Seasonal decor and holiday items

**Declutter prompts:** This is where things go to be forgotten. Be ruthless. Books you won't reread, decor you don't love, duplicate items that migrated here from other rooms.

---

### Living Room
**Estimated boxes: 6–12**

- [ ] Books (small boxes, labelled HEAVY)
- [ ] Media: DVDs, vinyl, gaming equipment (wrap electronics in anti-static bubble wrap if possible)
- [ ] Decorative items, candles, picture frames (wrap each in paper; frames go in mirror/picture boxes or between two pieces of foam)
- [ ] Throw blankets and pillows (use as filler in furniture gaps on the truck)
- [ ] Electronics: TV (original box if you have it; otherwise a TV box from a moving supply store), gaming consoles, speakers, routers (take photos of all cable setups before unplugging)
- [ ] Cables and remotes (label each cable with masking tape; bag remotes per device)
- [ ] Furniture (sofa, coffee table, bookshelves — photograph assembly instructions if you're disassembling)
- [ ] Rugs (roll tightly and secure with rope or plastic wrap; they go on the truck last/first off)

**Declutter prompts:** Furniture is the highest cost item to move by weight and cubic feet. If a piece is worn, cheap to replace, or doesn't suit your Oregon vision, sell it now. Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist move furniture fast.

---

### Bathrooms (all)
**Estimated boxes: 2–4 total**

Pack these last — you need them every day until moving day.

- [ ] Medications (carry these in the car — temperature extremes in a truck can degrade them)
- [ ] Toiletries (seal everything in zip-lock bags; pumps and liquid lids leak under pressure changes and jostling)
- [ ] Hair tools and accessories
- [ ] Towels (great box filler and padding around fragile items)
- [ ] Cleaning supplies (check what your mover permits; most flammable or corrosive products can't go on the truck)
- [ ] First aid kit (keep this in the car)
- [ ] Extra toilet paper (keep a roll out until literally the last moment)

**Declutter prompts:** Expired medications (dispose of properly at a pharmacy drop-box, not the trash or toilet), half-empty products you won't finish, duplicate tools.

---

### Home Office
**Estimated boxes: 4–8**

- [ ] Computer equipment (use original boxes if you have them; otherwise double-box electronics with foam or clothing padding)
- [ ] Monitors (buy monitor boxes from a moving store — worth it)
- [ ] External drives, USB hubs, peripherals
- [ ] Important documents (transport in the car — see the documents list from phase one)
- [ ] Books and binders
- [ ] Desk supplies (consolidate aggressively; most office supplies are cheap to replace)
- [ ] Printer (ink cartridges can leak — remove them and bag them separately)
- [ ] Cables (photograph setups before unplugging; label every cable)
- [ ] Artwork and diplomas (wrap and use picture boxes)

**Declutter prompts:** Old paperwork is the enemy. Shred anything financial that's more than 7 years old. Scan and digitize documents you want to keep but rarely touch. Recycle old cables, tech accessories, and anything that's been "I'll deal with that later" for over a year.

---

### Garage / Storage / Basement
**Estimated boxes: varies wildly — budget 10–20+ for a typical garage**

This is usually the most time-consuming and most declutter-able space. Start here.

- [ ] Tools (wrap blades and sharp edges; group by type)
- [ ] Hardware (sort and label — a tackle box or small bin works well for screws, bolts, anchors)
- [ ] Sporting and outdoor equipment (bikes, kayaks, camping gear — photograph for insurance before loading)
- [ ] Seasonal items (lawn equipment, holiday decorations, fans/space heaters)
- [ ] Cleaning equipment (mops, brooms, vacuums)
- [ ] Moving hazmat checklist: paint, propane tanks, gasoline, batteries, pesticides, and pool chemicals typically cannot go on a moving truck. Use them up, dispose of them properly at a hazmat drop-off, or donate them to neighbors.
- [ ] Garden hoses, tools, pots (consider whether the Oregon outdoor space warrants them)

**Declutter prompts:** Be honest about what you actually used in Ohio. Cross-country moves are priced partly by weight and volume. A lawn mower, a bag of potting soil, and a leaky garden hose are expensive to move and cheap to replace.

---

### Dog's Stuff
**Keep accessible throughout — do not pack in the truck**

- [ ] Food and treats (a 1–2 week supply in a sealed container that travels in the car)
- [ ] Water and bowls
- [ ] Leash, collar, harness, and tags
- [ ] Crate or bed (the dog may need this during packing chaos — keep it out until the last moment)
- [ ] Favorite toy and blanket (familiar smells reduce anxiety)
- [ ] Poop bags, paper towels, cleaning spray
- [ ] Medications and calming aids (keep these at room temperature in the car)
- [ ] Vet records pouch (keep with your documents, in the car)
- [ ] A printed card with the dog's name, your phone number, and your Oregon destination address (tape inside the crate and keep one in your wallet)

---

## A Note on Box Quantities

The estimates above assume a 2-bedroom household with a moderate amount of stuff. The real variable is books, clothing, and kitchen gear. If you're heavy on any of those, add 20–30% to that room's count. Total for a 2BR household typically runs 60–100 boxes. If you're over 80, that's a good reason to declutter harder.

---

---

# Services and Subscriptions: Cancellation and Transfer Timeline

The rule of thumb is to give providers more notice than you think you need, because holds, billing cycles, and contracts create friction. When in doubt, call rather than relying on an app.

---

## 8 Weeks Out — Research and Notify

- **Internet/cable:** Contact your Ohio provider. Ask about contract termination fees and the exact cancellation process. Research Oregon providers at the new address *now* — fiber availability varies and installation wait times can be 2–3 weeks. Book the Oregon install as soon as you have a confirmed move date. *(Joint)*
- **Renter's insurance:** Call your insurer. Ask whether the policy can be transferred to Oregon or needs to be cancelled and restarted. Get a quote for the Oregon address. *(Joint)*
- **Health insurance:** If employer-provided, confirm coverage continues during and after the move. If individual (ACA marketplace), research Oregon plans. A move is a qualifying life event, so you have a special enrollment window. *(Joint)*
- **Gym membership:** Check your contract. Many national gyms (Planet Fitness, LA Fitness) allow transfer to a local club. Local gyms usually require cancellation. Give the required notice. *(M or P)*
- **Vehicle insurance:** Notify your insurer of the move date. Ask what changes when you register in Oregon and whether you need to switch to an Oregon-based policy. Update as soon as registration changes. *(M)*

---

## 6 Weeks Out — Start Cancellations with Long Lead Times

- **Storage unit (Ohio):** Give notice per your contract. Clear it before the move. *(Joint)*
- **Newspaper or local subscriptions:** Cancel or update address. *(M or P)*
- **Professional memberships:** Update your address with any state bar, licensing board, or professional organization. Some licenses need to transfer to Oregon. *(M or P)*
- **HSA/FSA:** Notify your administrator of the address change. *(Joint)*
- **Bank accounts:** Update your address online or in-branch. If you use a local Ohio-only bank, consider whether to open a national account or Oregon credit union now so it's ready when you arrive. *(Joint)*
- **Investment accounts and retirement:** Update address. These will also need to be updated for tax documents. *(Joint)*
- **Life insurance:** Update beneficiary address info and notify of the move. *(Joint)*
- **Pet insurance:** Transfer or update address. *(M)*

---

## 4 Weeks Out — Address Change Wave

File your USPS change of address (usps.com) about 2 weeks before the move date, so it activates on time. Then notify the following directly (USPS forwarding is a backup, not a plan):

- [ ] Social Security Administration (ssa.gov)
- [ ] IRS (file Form 8822; can also update with next year's return but proactive is better)
- [ ] All banks and credit unions
- [ ] All credit card companies
- [ ] Mortgage servicer or student loan servicer
- [ ] Investment accounts (Fidelity, Vanguard, Schwab, etc.)
- [ ] Ohio BMV (address update on license before you leave; Oregon will replace it)
- [ ] Voter registration (Ohio cancellation is handled automatically when you register in Oregon)
- [ ] Employer payroll and HR
- [ ] Your accountant or tax preparer
- [ ] Alumni associations, professional organizations
- [ ] Magazine and subscription box services
- [ ] Amazon, eBay, and any e-commerce accounts you buy from regularly
- [ ] PayPal, Venmo, Cash App (less critical but billing address matters for some)
- [ ] Pharmacy — transfer all prescriptions to a national chain (CVS, Walgreens) or confirm your Oregon pharmacy can receive records

---

## 2 Weeks Out — Schedule Utility Shutoffs and Starts

- **Ohio electric:** Schedule shutoff for the day after move-out. *(M)*
- **Ohio gas:** Same. *(M)*
- **Ohio water:** Notify the city. *(M)*
- **Ohio internet/cable:** Schedule cancellation for the day after move-out. Return equipment before you leave. *(Joint)*
- **Ohio trash:** Cancel pickup. *(M)*
- **Oregon electric:** Confirm start date. *(M)*
- **Oregon gas:** Confirm start date. *(M)*
- **Oregon internet:** Confirm installation appointment and that it falls before your first full day there. *(Joint)*
- **Ohio alarm or security system:** Cancel or transfer. Contract buyout may apply. *(Joint)*
- **Ohio HOA:** If applicable, notify and confirm dues are current. *(Joint)*

---

## Moving Week — Final Cuts

- [ ] Cancel any meal kit deliveries (HelloFresh, etc.) or pause until Oregon address is set up
- [ ] Cancel or redirect any recurring deliveries (pet food subscriptions, Amazon Subscribe & Save)
- [ ] Update streaming services (Netflix, Hulu, etc.) with new billing address
- [ ] Update your phone carrier's billing address
- [ ] Confirm your Ohio utilities are scheduled for shutoff
- [ ] Confirm your Ohio internet equipment is returned and the account is closed

---

## First 2 Weeks in Oregon — Finish the List

- [ ] Confirm all Ohio services are terminated and final bills are paid
- [ ] Get Oregon renter's or homeowner's insurance active
- [ ] Register vehicles (Oregon DMV)
- [ ] Update driver's license
- [ ] Find a local pharmacy and transfer prescriptions
- [ ] Update voter registration (auto-registered via DMV in Oregon — confirm)
- [ ] Update

# 6–8 Week Phone-Syncable Calendar

**How to use this:** Your move day is Day 0. All dates below are relative to that. To use in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook, replace "Day 0" with your actual move date and count backward. Each entry includes a suggested reminder time and who's responsible. For recurring items, set them to repeat as noted.

For Google Calendar: create a new calendar called "Move 2025" so you can toggle it on and off without cluttering your main view. Set each event to "all day" with a notification at 8am.

---

## WEEK 8 (56 days before move day)

**Day -56 | Morning | Joint**
Book Oregon internet installation today.
*Reminder text: "Book Oregon internet NOW — installs book out 2–3 weeks"*

**Day -55 | Morning | Joint**
Get 3–4 moving quotes (movers or truck rental). Verify USDOT numbers.
*Reminder text: "Request moving quotes — verify USDOT at FMCSA.dot.gov"*

**Day -54 | Morning | M**
Schedule pre-move car maintenance (oil, tires, brakes, battery).
*Reminder text: "Book car service appointment for the drive to Oregon"*

**Day -53 | Morning | M**
Vet appointment for dog: health check, full records copy, rabies certificate, discuss travel anxiety meds.
*Reminder text: "Dog vet visit — get all records, rabies cert, travel meds conversation"*

**Day -52 | Morning | Joint**
Research Oregon neighborhoods, rentals, and commute. Set housing budget.
*Reminder text: "Oregon housing research — set budget, start applications"*

**Day -50 | Morning | Joint**
Check lease end date and notice requirements. Draft written notice to landlord.
*Reminder text: "Review lease — draft and send notice to landlord"*

---

## WEEK 7 (49 days before move day)

**Day -49 | Morning | Joint**
Book temporary dog-friendly housing in Oregon if permanent place isn't ready.
*Reminder text: "Book Oregon temp housing — confirm pet policy and fees"*

**Day -48 | Morning | Joint**
Select and book movers or truck. Read valuation/insurance coverage carefully before signing.
*Reminder text: "Book movers or truck — read Full Value Protection clause"*

**Day -47 | Morning | M**
If shipping vehicle: get 2–3 carrier quotes. Book open or enclosed transport.
*Reminder text: "Vehicle shipping quotes — book carrier if shipping"*

**Day -46 | Morning | Joint**
Begin declutter: garage, storage, guest room. Sell or donate large furniture you won't move.
*Reminder text: "Start declutter — garage and storage first. Post furniture on Marketplace."*

**Day -45 | Morning | Joint**
Order packing supplies: boxes, tape, bubble wrap, markers, sticker dots for label system.
*Reminder text: "Order packing supplies — small boxes for books, dish-pack cells for glasses"*

**Day -44 | Morning | Joint**
Gather all important documents into one folder (see documents list). Store in a bag that travels in the car.
*Reminder text: "Gather documents: titles, leases, dog records, passports, insurance, prescriptions"*

---

## WEEK 6 (42 days before move day)

**Day -42 | Morning | Joint**
Send formal written notice to Ohio landlord if not done. Request move-out inspection date.
*Reminder text: "Landlord written notice — request move-out inspection and deposit return"*

**Day -41 | Morning | M**
Contact Ohio internet/cable provider. Ask about contract exit fees. Schedule cancellation for day after move.
*Reminder text: "Ohio internet — get cancellation date, ask about equipment return"*

**Day -40 | Morning | Joint**
Contact renter's or homeowner's insurance. Ask about transfer to Oregon or new policy. Get quote.
*Reminder text: "Insurance — transfer or cancel Ohio policy, get Oregon quote"*

**Day -39 | Morning | M**
Contact vehicle insurer. Ask about out-of-state coverage during the move and Oregon registration requirements.
*Reminder text: "Auto insurance — confirm Oregon coverage, ask about policy transfer"*

**Day -38 | Morning | Joint**
Check gym, storage unit, and subscription contracts for cancellation notice requirements. Cancel or give notice as needed.
*Reminder text: "Cancel: gym, storage unit, local subscriptions — check required notice periods"*

**Day -37 | Morning | Joint**
Begin packing guest room and storage areas. Label all boxes: Room / Priority / Fragility.
*Reminder text: "Pack guest room and storage — use Room / Priority / Fragility label system"*

---

## WEEK 5 (35 days before move day)

**Day -35 | Morning | Joint**
File USPS change of address at usps.com. Set activation date for 2 days before move day.
*Reminder text: "File USPS change of address — activate 2 days before move day"*

**Day -34 | Morning | Joint**
Notify banks, credit cards, investment accounts, and retirement accounts of new address.
*Reminder text: "Address change wave: banks, credit cards, Fidelity/Vanguard, 401k"*

**Day -33 | Morning | Joint**
Notify: Social Security Administration, IRS (Form 8822), employer payroll and HR.
*Reminder text: "Address change: SSA, IRS Form 8822, employer HR and payroll"*

**Day -32 | Morning | Joint**
Notify: Amazon, subscription boxes, pharmacies. Transfer prescriptions to a national chain (CVS, Walgreens) or confirm Oregon pharmacy.
*Reminder text: "Address change: Amazon, subscriptions, pharmacy — transfer prescriptions"*

**Day -31 | Morning | M**
Research Oregon DMV requirements: documents needed for new license and vehicle registration. Note any emissions test requirement for your Oregon county.
*Reminder text: "Oregon DMV research — gather title, proof of residency, insurance for registration"*

**Day -30 | Morning | M**
Dog: order updated ID tags with new Oregon phone number or a temporary tag with destination address.
*Reminder text: "Order dog ID tags with new phone number — arrives before move day"*

---

## WEEK 4 (28 days before move day)

**Day -28 | Morning | Joint**
Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs: electric, gas, water, trash — for the day after move day.
*Reminder text: "Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs for [move day + 1]"*

**Day -27 | Morning | Joint**
Confirm Oregon utility start dates: electric, gas, water. Confirm internet installation appointment.
*Reminder text: "Confirm Oregon utility starts and internet install appointment"*

**Day -26 | Morning | Joint**
Pack living room: electronics, media, books, decor. Photograph all cable setups before unplugging.
*Reminder text: "Pack living room — photo all cable setups before unplugging"*

**Day -25 | Morning | Joint**
Pack home office: computers, monitors, files. Transport documents and hard drives in the car, not the truck.
*Reminder text: "Pack office — drives and documents travel in car, not truck"*

**Day -24 | Morning | Joint**
Sell, donate, or schedule pickup for any remaining unwanted furniture or large items.
*Reminder text: "Last call: sell or donate furniture. Schedule Habitat for Humanity pickup if needed."*

**Day -23 | Morning | M**
Dog: confirm overnight lodging is dog-friendly for each night of the drive. Confirm pet fees are paid or reserved.
*Reminder text: "Confirm dog-friendly lodging for each drive night — confirm pet fees"*

---

## WEEK 3 (21 days before move day)

**Day -21 | Morning | Joint**
Confirm mover appointment: arrival window, crew size, elevator/parking access, payment method.
*Reminder text: "Confirm movers — arrival window, payment, parking/elevator access"*

**Day -20 | Morning | Joint**
Pack primary bedroom: off-season clothing first, then wardrobe boxes for hanging items. Leave daily essentials out.
*Reminder text: "Pack bedroom — wardrobe boxes for hanging clothes, leave daily items out"*

**Day -19 | Morning | Joint**
Take photos or video of all valuables and their serial numbers. Back up to phone and a USB drive.
*Reminder text: "Photo inventory of valuables and serial numbers — back up to USB drive"*

**Day -18 | Morning | M**
If shipping vehicle: confirm carrier pickup date and location. Remove all personal items from the car.
*Reminder text: "Vehicle shipping: confirm pickup date, remove all personal items from car"*

**Day -17 | Morning | Joint**
Cancel or pause: meal kit deliveries, recurring Amazon orders, any subscriptions tied to Ohio address.
*Reminder text: "Cancel/pause: HelloFresh, Subscribe & Save, local recurring deliveries"*

**Day -16 | Morning | Joint**
Pack garage and storage: sort tools, dispose of hazmat (paint, propane, pesticides) at a local drop-off.
*Reminder text: "Pack garage — take hazmat to drop-off site. Can't go on truck."*

---

## WEEK 2 (14 days before move day)

**Day -14 | Morning | Joint**
Pack everything except daily essentials and the moving day kit. Each room should have a "Last Out" box clearly labeled.
*Reminder text: "Final packing push — every room except daily essentials and moving day kit"*

**Day -13 | Morning | M**
Dog: pack the travel bag. Food, water, bowls, leash, crate or travel bed, vet records, meds, calming aids, favorite toy, poop bags.
*Reminder text: "Pack dog travel bag — vet records pouch in car documents folder"*

**Day -12 | Morning | Joint**
Defrost and clean refrigerator. Use up or donate remaining perishable food.
*Reminder text: "Defrost fridge — donate perishables to neighbors or food bank"*

**Day -11 | Morning | M**
Confirm car is serviced, gas tank is full, and emergency kit is packed (see moving day one-pager).
*Reminder text: "Car check: oil, tires, gas, emergency kit loaded"*

**Day -10 | Morning | Joint**
Walk through every room and confirm all boxes are labeled. Check under beds, in closets, in cabinets, behind doors.
*Reminder text: "Full walkthrough — under beds, closets, cabinets, behind every door"*

**Day -9 | Morning | Joint**
Confirm all address changes are complete. Check bank statements and subscriptions for any you missed.
*Reminder text: "Final address change audit — scan recent mail and bank statements for missed accounts"*

---

## WEEK 1 (7 days before move day)

**Day -7 | Morning | Joint**
Confirm Ohio internet/cable cancellation and arrange equipment return (drop-off or scheduled pickup).
*Reminder text: "Ohio internet: return equipment, confirm cancellation date"*

**Day -6 | Morning | M**
Dog: test the car with a 30–60 min practice drive if travel anxiety meds are new. Confirm meds dosing with vet.
*Reminder text: "Dog practice drive — confirm medication dosing with vet"*

**Day -5 | Morning | Joint**
Return any borrowed items. Collect any items lent to others. Return library books.
*Reminder text: "Return borrowed items — collect anything lent out. Return library books."*

**Day -4 | Morning | Joint**
Confirm lodging for each night of the drive. Save confirmation numbers in a Notes doc.
*Reminder text: "Confirm all drive-route lodging — save confirmation numbers offline"*

**Day -3 | Morning | Joint**
Disassemble furniture that needs it. Keep hardware in labeled zip-lock bags taped to each piece.
*Reminder text: "Disassemble furniture — bag and tape hardware to each piece"*

**Day -2 | Morning | Joint**
Pack the moving day car kit: essentials bag, documents folder, dog bag, medications, snacks, phone chargers, valuables. See one-pager.
*Reminder text: "Pack car kit — documents, dog bag, meds, valuables, snacks, chargers. Nothing essential in the truck."*

**Day -1 | Morning | Joint**
Walk every room one final time. Pack the Last Out boxes. Load the car tonight if possible.
*Reminder text: "Final walkthrough. Pack Last Out boxes. Load car tonight."*

**Day -1 | Evening | M**
Give the dog a good long walk. Familiar routine helps reduce anxiety. Confirm tomorrow's start time.
*Reminder text: "Long dog walk tonight — familiar routine before the big day"*

---

## MOVE DAY — Day 0

**Day 0 | 7:00am | Joint**
Movers arrive or truck pickup. Have the inventory list and Bill of Lading ready.
*Reminder text: "Movers arrive — have inventory and Bill of Lading ready. Don't sign blank forms."*

**Day 0 | During | M**
Keep dog in a crate or quiet room away from movers. Give familiar toy and blanket.
*Reminder text: "Dog: crate in quiet room during loading — familiar toy and blanket"*

**Day 0 | Before leaving | Joint**
Final meter reads and photos. Return keys, remotes, and fobs. Get written receipt.
*Reminder text: "Meter read photos. Return all keys and remotes. Get written receipt."*

**Day 0 | Departure | Joint**
Take a video walk of every empty room, closet, and outdoor space for deposit documentation.
*Reminder text: "Video walkthrough of every empty room before you leave"*

---

## POST-MOVE REMINDERS (Oregon)

**Day +1 | Morning | Joint**
Photograph the new place at move-in. Email damage notes to landlord within 24 hours.
*Reminder text: "Photo Oregon move-in — email damage notes to landlord today"*

**Day +1 | Morning | Joint**
Confirm all utilities are on. Test internet. Locate breaker box, water shutoff, and gas shutoff.
*Reminder text: "Confirm utilities on — locate breaker, water shutoff, gas shutoff"*

**Day +3 | Morning | M**
Dog: first Oregon vet visit if scheduled. Update microchip registry with new address.
*Reminder text: "Dog vet visit — update microchip registry with Oregon address"*

**Day +7 | Morning | Joint**
Oregon DMV: get driver's licenses and register vehicles. Bring title, proof of residency, proof of insurance.
*Reminder text: "Oregon DMV — licenses and vehicle registration. Bring title, insurance, proof of residency."*

**Day +7 | Morning | M**
Get Oregon dog license from county or city office.
*Reminder text: "Oregon dog license — county or city office"*

**Day +14 | Morning | Joint**
Confirm all Ohio utilities and services have issued final bills and are closed.
*Reminder text: "Ohio utility audit — confirm all accounts closed, final bills paid"*

**Day +14 | Morning | Joint**
Confirm Ohio security deposit return timeline with landlord. Follow up in writing if not received.
*Reminder text: "Security deposit — follow up with Ohio landlord in writing if not received"*

**Day +30 | Morning | M**
Confirm Ohio vehicle registration is cancelled after Oregon registration is complete.
*Reminder text: "Cancel Ohio vehicle registration — confirm Oregon plates received"*

---

---

# Moving Day Essentials — Printable One-Pager

*Print this. Keep it in the front seat. This is your day-of reference.*

---

## 🚗 IN THE CAR (not the truck)

**Documents Pouch**
- [ ] Driver's licenses and passports
- [ ] Vehicle title, registration, insurance card
- [ ] Ohio lease and Oregon lease or closing papers

### Ohio → Oregon | Keep This in the Front Seat

---

## ⭐ TOP 3 PRIORITIES

1. **Never put documents, medications, or valuables in the truck.** If it's irreplaceable, it rides with you.
2. **Dog stays in a crate or quiet room away from movers until the truck is loaded and you're ready to leave.**
3. **Do not sign a blank or incomplete Bill of Lading.** Note any damage on the inventory before signing.

---

## 🚗 IN THE CAR — Documents Pouch *(J — load the night before)*

- [ ] Driver's licenses and passports (both)
- [ ] Vehicle title, registration, and insurance card
- [ ] Ohio lease + move-out receipt / Oregon lease or closing papers
- [ ] Moving contract, Bill of Lading, and inventory list
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt and carrier contact *(if applicable)*
- [ ] **Dog:** rabies certificate, vaccine records, microchip number, vet contact, medication list
- [ ] Prescriptions and current medications (both people)
- [ ] Birth certificates and Social Security cards
- [ ] Insurance policy numbers (auto, renters, health)
- [ ] Laptop, external hard drives, USB backup
- [ ] Jewelry and irreplaceable valuables
- [ ] Cash and a backup credit card

---

## 🧳 ESSENTIALS BAG — Open Tonight in Oregon *(J — pack the night before)*

- [ ] 2 changes of clothes each + one layer for mountain pass cold
- [ ] Toiletries: toothbrushes, soap, deodorant, face wash
- [ ] Phone chargers and a portable battery pack
- [ ] Medications for the next 3 days (keep accessible, not buried)
- [ ] Snacks, reusable water bottles, and a small cooler
- [ ] Paper towels, toilet paper (at least one roll — Oregon place may have none)
- [ ] Hand soap and dish soap
- [ ] One set of bed linens and a pillow each *(or sleeping bag as backup)*
- [ ] Coffee maker and supplies if you can't function without it *(M)*

---

## 🐾 DOG BAG — Accessible at All Times *(M — responsible throughout)*

- [ ] Food (2–3 day supply in a sealed container) and treats
- [ ] Collapsible water bowl and a full water bottle
- [ ] Leash, harness, and collar with updated ID tag
- [ ] Crate or travel bed and one familiar blanket
- [ ] Favorite toy
- [ ] Poop bags and cleaning spray
- [ ] Calming aids or travel anxiety medication *(confirm dosing with vet by Day -6)*
- [ ] Printed card: dog's name, your cell, Oregon destination address *(tape one inside crate)*

**Dog timing notes:**
- **Morning:** Crate the dog before movers arrive. Keep in a quiet room with water, toy, and blanket. *(M)*
- **During loading:** Check on the dog every 30–45 min. Keep the room closed. *(M)*
- **Departure:** Walk the dog before getting in the car. First break within 2 hours. *(M)*
- **On the road:** Stop every 2–3 hours — walk, water, and a few minutes off-leash if safe. Never leave the dog alone in a parked car in heat. *(M)*
- **Overnight:** Confirm pet policy at check-in. Set up the crate first so the dog has a familiar space immediately. *(M)*

---

## 🏠 BEFORE YOU LEAVE — Final Walkthrough *(J)*

- [ ] Photograph or video every empty room, closet, cabinet, and outdoor space
- [ ] Read all utility meters and photograph them
- [ ] Check: under every bed, inside every cabinet, behind every door, in the attic or basement
- [ ] Return all keys, fobs, garage remotes, and mailbox keys — get a written receipt *(J)*
- [ ] Confirm Ohio utility shutoffs are scheduled for today or tomorrow *(M)*
- [ ] Sign and keep a copy of the Bill of Lading — note any damage before signing *(J)*

- [ ] Gas tank full before leaving *(M)*

- [ ] Lodging confirmation numbers saved offline *(P)*

- [ ] Walk through the new place and photograph everything before unloading
